elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 2.2 as rendered reads "Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term," replacing the "sole and exclusive provider" commitment. No requirements, all-of-its-requirements, or third-party-procurement prohibition binds Customer anywhere else, and Section 12.3 is retained confirming Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." Deterministic check "no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains" returns ok.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no exclusivity obligation on Customer at all, so a category limitation is unnecessary; the preferred outcome exceeds this fallback constraint.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity period exists following the change of Section 2.2 to "a non-exclusive provider," so no duration cap is required.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no exclusivity to terminate on a service-level failure, so a performance-based exit is moot.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no exclusivity obligation survives, so a delivery-date exit trigger is unnecessary.

reasons: The single operative change is confined to the four words creating the restriction in Section 2.2 ("sole and exclusive provider" becomes "a non-exclusive provider"); the remainder of the sentence, including "throughout the term," is retained, and no other clause was touched, paraphrased, or deleted.
The edit reaches the preferred level with one operation and adds no extras (no survival tail, no procedure, no new covenant), so it is minimal for a presence-kind rule.

Favourable existing language is retained: Section 12.3's no-exclusivity acknowledgement and Customer's freedom to engage any supplier are left intact, and the edit removes the internal contradiction between Sections 2.2 and 12.3 rather than creating one.

No undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence results; Vendor remains an appointed provider of the Services under the Order Forms, so pricing, term, and delivery mechanics are unaffected.

The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: the original Section 2.2 imposed full-term exclusive dealing with no category limit, no 12-month cap, and no performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory under the rule.
